extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals and teams preparing entries for the PRSA Anvil Awards (Western District/ national entrants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and assembling a competitive Anvil Award submission, including the entry summary, supporting materials, alignment to judging criteria, and visual/readability considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell a compelling story (entry summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The one- or two-page summary of an entry is the most important and influential component of a submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell a compelling, concise and straightforward story, outlining the most critical points for the judge. The summary does not need to include every detail of your campaign or tactic, but the entry should be neat and complete — don’t leave any plot holes that you don’t explain in your entry. As a bonus tip, avoid local references, as the Anvils are judged by individuals from around the country who may not pick up on geographic mentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep the entry summary to one or two pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should include a one- or two-page summary as the primary narrative component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on concise storytelling and prioritize the most critical points; omit extraneous detail while ensuring completeness (no unexplained 'plot holes').

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid local references
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on geographic or highly local references in your summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because judges are from around the country, local references may not be understood — remove or explain them so the entry reads clearly to a national audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use research to support and inform the campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs that stand out often used research to inform messages, strategies and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details if you’ve done primary or secondary research. Demonstrate how you leveraged research to inform your efforts — showing the link between research and strategy/implementation is critical to making a campaign award-worthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match your content to the published judging criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the judging criteria readily available to all submitters to understand where judges will put emphasis and how they’ll score an entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review scoring valuations and important reminders of what to include and not include. Use the answer key to align and 'match' your content to what judges will be grading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include and organize supporting materials as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting materials (separate uploads) should act as visual aids and proof points to validate claims in the summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you reference a plan, research, a media hit or a metrics report in your summary, include it in the supporting materials. Organize those materials to align with the section headers so a judge can easily navigate to proof points and validate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make your entry judge-friendly (readability & visual presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should be easy to read and pleasant to the eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize dense content with bullets and subheads, bold critical lines and phrases, and break up copy so it’s digestible. Taking time to make the entry compelling both narratively and visually can help it stand out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the appropriate award level/category (Silver vs. Bronze)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the distinction between award types so you submit in the right category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Silver Anvil Awards celebrate the best strategic PR campaigns of the year, while Bronze Anvil Awards recognize outstanding PR tactics that contribute to overall program or campaign success — select the category that matches whether your entry is a full strategic campaign or a tactic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide complete, neat submissions (no missing elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should be neat and complete and not omit critical explanatory elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though summaries are concise, ensure no essential explanation is missing; incomplete submissions or missing proof points (e.g., lack of supporting materials for claimed results) weaken an entry.
